system_description.narrative_title: U.S.–Iran escalation disrupts global energy and maritime flows
system_description.narrative_summary: A cycle of strikes, counter-strikes and maritime threats in the Gulf — involving the U.S., Iran and regional proxies — is disrupting oil production, shipping through chokepoints and global energy markets. The system is open: military actions, sanctions, trade rerouting and market expectations interact across borders, producing feedbacks (attacks → shipping disruption → higher oil prices → economic and political pressure → more coercive measures) that amplify systemic volatility. Secondary responses (alternative routes, reserves draws, refinery shifts, sanctions on finance/airlines) create new linkages that redistribute risk across global trade, finance and energy infrastructure.
system_description.scope: Within the boundary: military and proxy strikes in the Gulf and adjoining seas, maritime traffic through chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, regional routes; relevant impacts on Panama Canal), attacks on energy infrastructure (refineries, Aramco facilities, tankers), shipping industry operations and safety protocols, oil and refined-product markets and prices, refiners' product allocation, strategic petroleum reserves, sanctions and financial flows affecting Iran and regional trade, and immediate policy responses by Gulf states, the U.S. and international maritime authorities.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic system (energy security, international trade/maritime order, and financial sanctions regimes)
adjacent_subsystems: Regional security and military posture (U.S., Iran, Gulf states, proxies/Houthis)
Global maritime logistics & chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Panama Canal, ports, shipping insurers)
International finance & sanctions enforcement (banks, trade finance, aviation/insurance)
evidence_headlines: Oil Rises Amid Escalation in U.S.-Iran Conflict
Hormuz traffic dips to lowest since May after US, Iranian strikes on ships
Saudi Aramco facility hit in new strikes
UAE builds alternative trade, energy routes after Iran attacks, official says
Global shipping rules are collapsing, say maritime nations
Oil Nears $100 a Barrel as Fresh Attacks on Saudi Energy Operations Raise Supply Concerns

variables.name: Conflict intensity
variables.description: Aggregate intensity of military and proxy strikes, counter-strikes and maritime attacks in the regional theatre.

variables.name: Maritime security risk
variables.description: Perceived and measured hazard level for commercial vessels operating in affected seas and chokepoints.

variables.name: Shipping throughput rate
variables.description: Volume of cargo and tanker transits through key regional sea lanes and chokepoints per unit time.

variables.name: Chokepoint utilization
variables.description: Proportion of available capacity of major maritime chokepoints being used at a given time.

variables.name: Oil supply disruption rate
variables.description: Rate at which crude oil and refined-product supply is lost or withheld from markets due to attacks, closures or production changes.

variables.name: Crude oil price level
variables.description: Market price level for benchmark crude oil reflecting current supply-demand and risk premia.

variables.name: Market volatility expectation
variables.description: Market-implied expectation of future price volatility for energy and related assets.

variables.name: Refined product availability
variables.description: Available inventory levels of gasoline, diesel and other refined products in relevant markets.

variables.name: Strategic reserve level
variables.description: Quantity of government-held strategic petroleum reserves available for release to markets.

variables.name: Insurance and freight premiums
variables.description: Risk-related uplift in marine insurance and freight rates applied to shipping in the affected region.

variables.name: Shipping rerouting rate
variables.description: Rate at which vessels alter routes to avoid risky zones, measured as additional transits or distance/time incurred per unit time.

variables.name: Financial sanctions intensity
variables.description: Degree to which financial restrictions impede payments, banking relationships and trade finance related to the actors affected by the conflict.

variables.name: Refinery operating rate
variables.description: Average utilization rate of refining capacity in markets affected by supply and logistical disruptions.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure damage
variables.description: Cumulative physical impairment to production, refining and export infrastructure from attacks and sabotage.

variables.name: Global trade flow volume
variables.description: Aggregate volume of maritime-dependent international trade passing through or affected by the regional routes per unit time.

variables.name: Political pressure on policymakers
variables.description: Level of domestic and international political pressure driving defensive, coercive or economic policy responses related to the conflict.

catalysts.title: Iran announces maritime exclusion/restricted zone
catalysts.description: Iran declares or enforces a new restricted/exclusion zone in the Gulf, altering legal navigation and triggering re-routing or interdiction of vessels.
catalysts.rationale: Grounded in: 'Iran says to announce new restricted zone in the Gulf in the coming days'; 'Iran warns of maritime exclusion zone.'

catalysts.title: Renewed Houthi attacks on Gulf energy and shipping
catalysts.description: Continued wave of Houthi strikes against Saudi energy facilities and ships, disrupting production and exports and sustaining regional escalation.
catalysts.rationale: Driven by: 'Wave of Houthi strikes halts work at energy facilities'; 'Saudi Aramco oil facilities hit in new strikes.'

catalysts.title: OPEC+ keeps output steady for October
catalysts.description: OPEC+ maintains its announced production policy for October, leaving announced supply unchanged during a period of elevated regional risk.
catalysts.rationale: Based on: 'OPEC+ keeps oil output policy unchanged for October.'

catalysts.title: Panama Canal transit cuts continue due to drought
catalysts.description: Additional slot reductions and transit cuts through the Panama Canal from drought and management changes reduce capacity and force rerouting.
catalysts.rationale: From: 'Shipping through Panama Canal faces new cuts as water dries up'; 'New Panama Canal Chief Must Navigate Drought and Geopolitics.'

catalysts.title: Further U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve draws
catalysts.description: Additional SPR releases or sales continue to support markets as administrations seek to blunt price spikes and supply shortages.
catalysts.rationale: Linked to: 'Oil stocks in US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fall by 1.2 million barrels to lowest level since 1982.'

catalysts.title: Sustained U.S. naval operations and strikes in region
catalysts.description: Continued U.S. naval presence and strikes (carrier operations, strikes on tankers/ships) maintain pressure and risk of further kinetic incidents.
catalysts.rationale: Supported by: 'U.S. military destroys five Iranian oil tankers'; 'US carrier Abraham Lincoln departs Thailand.'

catalysts.title: New rounds of sanctions and financial pressure on Iran
catalysts.description: Fresh U.S., UK and allied sanctions (banking, aviation) further restrict Iran's financial channels and trade finance linked to energy exports.
catalysts.rationale: Based on: 'US issues fresh Iran-related sanctions'; 'UK publishes legislation for tougher sanctions on Iran.'

catalysts.title: Iran raises domestic fuel prices
catalysts.description: Iran implements announced fuel price increases for consumers/heavy users, aggravating domestic shortages and social pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Cited by: 'Iran to raise petrol prices as US war triggers shortages'; 'Iran's government to raise fuel price for heavy users.'
